sentences.text: A prominent ridge running along the postorbital bone identifies Eogavialis as a member of the gavialid family.
The genus name Eogavialis was proposed by Eric Buffetaut in 1982 to reassign species previously placed in Tomistoma.
Some researchers argue that several species previously named under Tomistoma are junior synonyms of Eogavialis africanum because they are morphologically indistinguishable.
The earliest fossils date to the Priabonian stage of the late Eocene, between 37.2 and 33.9 million years ago, while the total record extends to the Messinian at 5.333 million years ago.
Specimens from Kenya push the known range into the late Miocene and early Pliocene, between 11.61 and 2.59 million years ago.
This animal likely inhabited broad, shallow, meandering rivers within its environment.
However, some fossils suggest it may have been adapted to coastal marine habitats, unlike most modern crocodilians.
